Decision: leave WriteChapters sequential, don't implement parallel. Measured on a real smoke test (9 chapters, karpathy/micrograd, direct Anthropic API bypassing caveman-proxy): sequential 562.3s vs parallel 521.0s, a ~7% wall-clock gain. Far short of the review's anticipated N-x speedup -- Anthropic's own per-account rate limits partially serialize concurrent calls, and wall-clock is bounded by the single slowest chapter. 7% doesn't justify the real costs: lost narrative continuity (chapters can no longer literally continue prior prose), max_workers=total needing a cap for larger repos, and retry semantics degrading from 'redo one chapter' to 'redo the whole fan-out'. Message Batches API also considered and ruled out separately -- it trades latency for cost (up to 1hr, max 24hr turnaround), wrong tradeoff for a single interactive tour generation. Working prototype (uncommitted, branch prototype/parallel-writechapters in agent worktree) available if repo size/chapter count grows enough to revisit.
